newsitem.title: USA: Fla. judge strips future damages from tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Fla. judge strips future damages from tobacco case.

text.p: A judge ruled Thursday that Florida cannot seek $16 billion in anticipated future damages it had sought in its lawsuit to recoup from tobacco companies the public health costs of treating smoking-related illnesses.
"The tobacco industry is correct in that the law does not allow for collecting now future damages," Judge Harold Cohen ruled.

Cohen's ruling still allows Florida to seek $1 billion in actual damages, as well as triple damages if it can prove the tobacco companies engaged in criminal conduct in the sale and advertising of cigarettes.
Cohen also encouraged the state to appeal the ruling quickly.

Because of "the great public importance of this issue -- and in light of the trial -- I encourage the state to make a quick appeal of this ruling so that if I am reversed future damages can be included in the case and we can proceed from there," Cohen said.

The ruling came during the third day of pre-trial review of the issues in the Medicaid case, as the judge sought to narrow what can be presented to the jury during the trial, which is expected to begin on Aug. 4.
